points.t: A child with a **brown or black, often hairy birthmark mole**, sometimes large with smaller **satellite** moles.
**Post-zygotic NRAS mutation** in melanocyte precursors; earlier mutation → larger naevus, more satellites.
Classify by **projected adult size**; refer large / giant or multiple CMN to paediatric dermatology; **MRI in infants with ≥ 2 CMN at birth**; teach families what change to report.
**Melanoma in large / giant CMN** (often deep or in childhood); **neurocutaneous melanosis**; psychological impact.

cause.lead: A mosaic: the earlier the mutation, the bigger the mark.
points: NRAS (BRAF in some small CMN) in neural-crest melanoblasts.
Early mutation → large naevus, satellites, **CNS melanocytes** (neurocutaneous melanosis).
Growth with the child: head lesions **~double**, trunk and limbs **~triple** to adulthood.
**Small < 1.5 cm; medium 1.5–20 cm; large 20–40 cm; giant > 40 cm.**
A **30 cm trunk CMN at age 5 projects to > 40 cm = giant**.
Brown to black, often hairy; becomes **rougher, lumpier, hairier or lighter** with time: benign maturation.
**New firm nodule, ulceration, rapid growth or pain** = urgent.
**Satellites / ≥ 2 CMN at birth**: markers of CNS involvement (seizures, delay, hydrocephalus).
Brain + spine, ideally < 6 months (natural sleep), if **≥ 2 CMN at birth, any size**; not routine for a single CMN without neurology.
**Small / medium: lifetime melanoma risk < 1%** (usually after puberty, at the edge).
**Large / giant: ~2–5%** (up to 10–15% if > 40 cm with many satellites); often **childhood and deep / CNS**.
Paediatric dermatology (routine; **urgent** for nodule, ulcer, rapid change) for lifelong MDT surveillance (dermatology, plastics, neurology, psychology).
Teach families what change to report; photograph regularly; sun protection; psychological support.

limits.t: No evidence it reduces melanoma risk in large / giant CMN.

items.t: New firm nodule, ulceration, rapid growth or pain within a CMN.
Scalp or multiple CMN with headaches, vomiting or seizures: same-day paediatrics.
≥ 2 CMN at birth or large / giant with satellites: MRI and specialist surveillance.

pearls.t: Rough, hairy, raised changes are expected. A **hard lump** is not.
Course “5–10%” applies to large / giant CMN, not small / medium.

quiz.q: A 30 cm trunk CMN at age 5: category?

quiz.a: Infants with ≥ 2 CMN at birth (any size).

quiz.q: Does prophylactic excision remove the risk?
